useCases.label: Meditation Timer
useCases.desc: A free 10-minute meditation timer with a gentle alarm. Set it, close your eyes, and it rings softly when your session ends.
useCases.intro: Sit, breathe, and let the timer keep track. This 10-minute meditation timer rings when you're done so you can stay present instead of watching the clock — adjust the minutes for a longer or shorter sit.

useCases.label: Study Timer
useCases.desc: A free 50-minute study timer with an alarm. Great for focused study blocks and exam revision. No sign-up.
useCases.intro: A 50-minute study block is long enough for deep work and short enough to stay sharp. Start the timer, study until it rings, then take a 10-minute break. Change the minutes to fit your own study rhythm.

useCases.label: Workout Timer
useCases.desc: A free 30-minute workout timer with an alarm. Keep your session on track from warm-up to cool-down.
useCases.intro: Set a 30-minute cap on your session and train without checking the clock — the alarm sounds when time's up. Adjust the minutes for a quick burst or a longer workout.

useCases.label: Tea Timer
useCases.desc: A free 4-minute tea steeping timer with an alarm. Brew the perfect cup without over-steeping.
useCases.intro: Most black teas steep for about 3–5 minutes and green teas a little less. Start this 4-minute timer when you pour, and it rings before your tea turns bitter — tweak the minutes for your blend.

useCases.label: Boiled Egg Timer
useCases.desc: A free online egg timer with an alarm. Set it for soft, medium or hard-boiled eggs and it rings when they're done.
useCases.intro: How long it takes to boil an egg depends on how you like it and how high up you are — pick a doneness below, then add a little time the higher your elevation.

useCases.label: Plank Timer
useCases.desc: A free 2-minute plank timer with an alarm. Hold your plank and let the timer count you down.
useCases.intro: Set the timer, get into position, and hold until it rings. Two minutes is a strong goal — start with 30–60 seconds and build up. Adjust the seconds to match your training.

useCases.label: 2-Minute Brushing Timer
useCases.desc: A free 2-minute timer for brushing teeth, with an alarm. Dentists recommend two minutes — perfect for kids and adults.
useCases.intro: Dentists recommend brushing for a full two minutes, twice a day. Start the timer and brush until it rings — a simple way to help kids (and grown-ups) brush long enough.
